title: Choose the visual world for the admin app
question: The roll assigned Accreditation Pass. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Accreditation Pass
options.lineage: Event accreditation passes and colour-coded lanyards
options.thesis: Every Profile is a pass for one venue: the address is the name printed on it, the Label is the venue, and its colour strip says whether it gets you in.
options.viewport: Cobalt lanyard band across the top holding the Label field and Create; below it the pass just issued, the address set huge on two lines with a green state strip and a Copy button you can hit with a thumb; the live list follows as slim passes, each with its state strip on the left.
options.risk: Passes are about being identified; the colour coding has to stay a state signal and never turn into decoration or a badge-maker toy.

raised.raise: State never rides on colour alone: a first-minute address carries a dotted strip, an out-of-sync list a hatched one.
Every rule is one device pixel and the palette holds three inks plus the state colours, nothing else.
One face at a committed scale ladder: the issued address is set at specimen size, never a bumped-up body line.

options.label: Private Bag Wall
options.lineage: Post office box banks: anodised doors, enamel numerals
options.thesis: The Profiles are a wall of numbered boxes on your own premises; each door carries its address and a flag when something needs you.
options.viewport: A dark enamel header with the Label field and Create; the new address shown as a box door with its number plate; live Profiles as a tight grid of doors on desktop and a stacked bank on a phone.
options.risk: Familiar: mail is the obvious reading of an email product, and most runs in this category land on a postal metaphor.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: Metro maps fired as enamel murals
options.thesis: Mail's route from Cloudflare to the server to your inbox is a line on a diagram, and every state is service status.
options.viewport: Midnight shell with the create field on top; a single route line shows sync health (live, arriving in about a minute, suspended); Profiles listed as stations on their line.
options.case: Holds product clarity (propagation and sync states map onto service status) but loses audience identification on a phone task that is mostly create and copy.
options.risk: The map can upstage a task that is really one text field and one Copy button.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Live and Retired as side A and side B of one folded card.
options.viewport: Side A lists live Profiles, flip to side B for Retired.
options.case: Too playful for a tool you open mid-signup; hand lettering slows reading an address.
options.kept: Live and Retired as hard halves with a clear switch, never one blended list.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Profiles as two columns of entries keyed down a vermilion rail.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns round a centre rail of keys.
options.case: Two columns and a margin apparatus fight a one-handed phone task.
options.kept: One-device-pixel rules and a strict three-ink limit.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not a tool.

options.label: Exposure Record Sheets
options.thesis: Overlapping sheets with hatch density for load and conflict.
options.case: Overlapping sheets add depth the task does not need.
options.kept: State drawn without colour: hatch and dotted marks alongside the hue.
options.risk: Visual noise on a small screen.

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Addresses set in coarse bitmap display type.
options.case: Pixel letterforms hurt reading an address you must copy exactly.
options.kept: A committed type scale with the address at specimen size.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms and layout built from one visible grid.
options.viewport: A visible grid with monumental type.
options.case: A visible grid is decoration on a page with one field and a list.
options.kept: A strict spacing module everything snaps to.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, neutral admin page like the best forwarding-address services ship, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar with the create field and button, the new address in a highlighted card, a plain table of Profiles below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other admin page; this is the SaaS look you said would feel wrong.
